chunks: Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, do you see the one who rejects this matter to me as if he has rejected you?' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad! The one who rejects this matter to you, so he has rejected against the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and against Allah, Blessed and High. O Abu Muhammad! The dead one from among you who was upon this matter is a martyr.' I said, 'Even if he died upon his bed?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, even if he died upon his bed, he is alive in the Presence of his Lord, being given Sustenance.'
ai.seo_question: Is a believer who dies naturally considered a martyr if they adhered to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the theological principle of 'rad' (rejection) by linking the rejection of the Imams' authority directly to the rejection of the Prophet and Allah, emphasizing the continuity of prophetic leadership. He further clarifies the status of the believer who adheres to this authority, affirming that such a person is considered a martyr (shahid) even if they die naturally in their bed, retaining spiritual vitality and sustenance from their Lord in the barzakh (intermediate realm).
